purpose: Release-admission requirements, not an installation catalog or completed qualification. Missing receipts and source decisions deliberately block promotion.
limitations: This is the initial declared engine/backend/checkpoint matrix; the full test census and final source/build freeze remain separate acceptance requirements.

Each row has one explicit operating system. Since September 29, 2026 the campaign admits macOS on Apple Silicon only: Linux/Windows CPU, CUDA, ROCm and Vulkan rows and the CUDA-only q27 track were removed as out of scope, not qualified. Scalar CPU reference tests on the Mac remain part of Metal numerical verification. Of the DeepSeek V4 Flash checkpoints only the Vision-Exp row remains; the four non-Vision rows were removed on the same date as out of scope.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B run on the bundled llama.cpp (b11836 since October 23, 2026; b11371 before) through the DStudio host; Chat, Agent and Cowork passed real inference on macOS Metal on October 3, 2026 on b11371, and Qwen3.6 passed again on b11836 on October 23 (tests/live/llama_resident_live_test.mjs). Design on llama.cpp models is not implemented. Linux and Windows llama.cpp builds are not qualified.
The former Qwen side engines (vagrillo/ds4 qwen35moe-support, Ninnix/q36) were retired on October 3, 2026; their tracks, patch sets and targets were removed.

The main track includes the complete f4d03f6..bd66c40 campaign delta and all 79 subsequent commits through 0aaea5a, including Qwen Next; on November 3, 2026 the pin moved to 890898c (160 further upstream commits, mainly DeepSeek V4.1 Metal/CUDA/TP work, Qwen PLE prefetch and server fixes), with the media-memory, M2 Max and Qwen candidate-preparation patches and Chat PLD rebased onto it. Installations at 0aaea5a are not upgraded in place. Managed upgrades have scoped receipts; full mode, numerical and earlier cross-fork qualification remains open.
A recorded tip only freezes the observed revision. The per-target source review must classify every commit; empty arrays are not equivalence claims.
Every declared target is macOS; the release command checks all of them.
V4.1 adds Metal-only Q2/Q4 candidates. Its weights, native disk Engram and expert streaming require distinct real-load and correctness evidence; new rows do not imply qualification.

q36's installer now targets 1305843 (upstream September 24): the reviewed 8362010 runtime rebased with three resolved conflicts, plus the unchanged monitor/monitor-owner/cache-usage patches; existing 8362010 and d67687e installs upgrade in place. Earlier 8362010 real-model receipts do not qualify the new binary. The Qwen3.6 fork additionally carries a Q6_K MoE shader correction.

Since upstream's September 14 merge (9139e2a), Qwen3.8 Flash Next is part of antirez/ds4 main; the active 890898c pin is upstream's November 2 revision. The retired fork and its separate Q4 PLE format are not active installer targets. New Q2/Q4 single-file BF16 n-gram releases need fresh real-model qualification; older fork receipts are historical, not relabeled.

Since October 22, 2026 the flash41-q2 target is the 1017 checkpoint: antirez's official DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf, the file upstream ds4 5379c1c's ds41f-q2 names. The vendored 890898c download_model.sh names it with the same published SHA-256 but follows the repository head; scripts/download-ds41-1017.sh downloads it at a pinned revision, together with the community 1017 vision sidecar (ds41f-1017-vision; antirez publishes none) whose source revision 1bae0e10 matches. patch/ds4-v41-vision-pairing (antirez/ds4 PR #1225, unmerged) pairs a V4.1 sidecar with the language GGUF by general.source.revision; it is a no-op once upstream drops the hard-coded df42c109 revision. Original-checkpoint receipts do not qualify the 1017 weights.

Since November 11, 2026 the MLX Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MXFP8 selection has a target. MLX is installed from verified PyPI wheels (src/engines/mlx), not built from an archive: its tracks record the upstream revisions those wheels were released from (mlx-lm 0.32.2 and mlx 0.32.4), with no later commit under review, and its patch set is the three versioned mlx-lm adaptations. The same day the three host-served targets (llama.cpp Qwen3.6, llama.cpp Qwen3.8-27B and MLX) gained the gates the campaign requires of every selection: numerics, quality-100, install-upgrade, learn, desktop and design-runtime, plus textual-isolation for the text-only ones and vision-pdf-50 for 27B. No receipt was added.

On November 11, 2026 thirteen patch-set entries (seven files of the main and Laguna sets) no longer matched their recorded SHA-256: the patches had changed without this manifest being refreshed, so the checker would have reported CONTENT_CHANGED. The hashes were refreshed to the files shipped at that commit. No receipt existed that was bound to the earlier patch-set digests.

On November 11, 2026 the 300 main-track commits of f4d03f6..890898c were classified for the nine targets that list main (scripts/engine-delta-review.mjs, docs/upstream/main-delta-2026-11-11.json). The classification is by changed path, against a file-by-file comparison of src/engines/ds4 with upstream 890898c (498 shipped files identical; 2990 declared omissions, none compiled or read by the macOS build): 243 integrated and 57 not applicable for each of the six ds4 main and two llama.cpp targets, the latter because their Agent, Cowork and Design frontends are built from the main checkout. Laguna, built from its own branch, has 57 not applicable and 243 left unclassified: whether it needs a main change is a source judgment. This is not a behavioural review and adds no receipt. The same day the remote refs of main, llama.cpp, mlx-lm and mlx were 116, 446, 18 and 82 commits past their recorded tips (b3f5018, aa75ff3, 56230fa, fc344c9); no pin was moved and those commits are not reviewed.
